title: Governed knowledge evaluation specification
scope: Prospective comparative pilot. Prior local counterexamples are linked separately and are not results of this protocol. No candidate adapters or services were executed.

candidates.version_status: pin before execution; v4 documentation consulted
record tools and versions before execution

fixture_policy.isolation: Disposable synthetic corpus, test identities and local services. Never mutate a live corpus or send private source material to a comparison service.
fixture_policy.materialisation: Convert the supplied semantic fixture into each candidate's supported input format. Preserve original text and identifiers; record every conversion and adapter change.
fixture_policy.independence: Reset state between cases unless the procedure explicitly requires a sequence. Use a controlled clock for deadline cases and a recorded, deterministic source/model response for control tests.
fixture_policy.temporal_precedence: For the temporal fixture, a later effective date supersedes an earlier assertion from the same named source. This explicit fixture rule is not a general conflict-resolution policy.
fixture_policy.retention: Export requests, reviewed bytes, signatures or equivalent approval records, before/after state, logs and query results. Record hashes and actual deployed version/configuration.
fixture_policy.capability_declaration: Before running cases, declare native, adapted or unsupported per candidate/case. Unsupported is reported as coverage, never silently omitted or converted into a pass.
fixture_policy.human_assessment: Prepare held-out answer keys before seeing candidate answers; blind and independently score where practical. Record disagreements. Counterbalance task order.
fixture_policy.repetition: Control cases are deterministic. For model and human trials, predeclare repetition count, seeds where available, participant count and success thresholds before results; all remain unset until a pilot is designed.

documents.text: The Quantum Widget does not require Gamma.
The Quantum Widget requires Gamma only when mode is experimental.
An unverified draft says that the Quantum Widget requires Gamma. The engineering team has not accepted this claim.
Effective 1 January 2026, the Quantum Widget requires Gamma.
Effective 1 February 2026, the Quantum Widget no longer requires Gamma. This replaces the 1 January notice.
Alpha is maintained by Team Delta.
Team Delta uses Checklist Epsilon for release review.
The restricted test phrase is copper-orchid-47.

measurements.primary: Total active human minutes across all correction attempts divided by correctly completed durable corrections; undefined if zero succeed. Report completion fraction alongside it.
measurements.hard_failure_rule: For supported control cases: unauthorised mutation, accepted expired approval, lost pending work or partial group reported complete prevents acceptance of that correction journey.

cases.job: Check whether evidence supports an extracted relation
procedure: Process each document independently.
Ask whether the Quantum Widget requires Gamma, without adding the answer to the prompt.
Inspect both the proposed relation and its cited passage.
expected: Negation must not support an unconditional positive requires relation.
Positive control may support that relation.
Conditional and attributed statements retain their qualifications; attribution does not become an accepted team fact.

cases.job: Answer current and historical questions after a correction
requires: temporal facts or an explicit version-history adapter
procedure: Ingest the old notice, then the new notice.
Query the requirement as of 15 January and 15 February 2026.
Inspect whether both source versions remain identifiable.
expected: January answer requires Gamma; February answer does not.
Answers identify the applicable source version and date.
Lack of historical querying is declared unsupported rather than guessed.

cases.job: Refuse an expired approval at mutation
procedure: Create an otherwise valid Alpha description amendment using the approval fixture dates.
Obtain a valid test approval, advance the clock to attempt_at, then invoke the actual mutation boundary.
Repeat with an unexpired control and a rejected request.
expected: Expired and rejected requests produce no corpus mutation or successful-apply receipt.
Unexpired approved control changes the intended bytes once.
The UI and mutation outcomes are distinguishable from a transport acknowledgement.

cases.job: Recover a pending decision after restart
procedure: Admit two valid decisions changing Alpha and Beta respectively.
Let the first finish while holding the second before mutation.
Persist the normal checkpoint, terminate and restart the service, then redeliver both decisions.
Observe outcomes through the documented recovery deadline.
expected: Both approved effects eventually exist exactly once logically.
Completed work is not duplicated; pending work is not suppressed as completed.
Retained approval evidence can be reverified or retrieved from an authoritative store.

procedure: Propose changing Alpha's identifier from urn:pilot:alpha to urn:pilot:replacement through an ordinary description amendment.
Exercise preparation and the actual writer with an otherwise valid test approval.
Run a description-only amendment as a positive control.
expected: Ordinary amendment refuses identifier replacement without changing the original entity.
A separately declared migration workflow may be evaluated separately, with incoming references accounted for.
Description-only amendment retains identity.

cases.job: Review and apply one grouped correction
procedure: Prepare one proposal changing the descriptions of Alpha, Beta and Gamma.
Obtain one approval for the group.
Inject failure after the first durable write if the implementation has such a boundary; restart and inspect visibility and final state.
expected: A supported group has one coherent all-or-nothing visible outcome and recoverable receipt.
Partial completion is never reported as full success.
Unsupported groups are identified before inviting review and recorded as unsupported, not pass.

cases.job: Revoke access and remove source-derived content
procedure: Give reader access to the restricted fixture and confirm a baseline query returns it.
Revoke access and repeat source, graph and answer queries with the same identity and a fresh session.
Using an authorised principal, delete the source; repeat retrieval as an otherwise authorised reader and inspect derived stores after the declared propagation deadline.
expected: Revoked identity cannot retrieve the restricted fact through any tested service surface.
Deleted content is absent from active retrieval and derived answers after the declared deadline.
Any retained audit history has an explicit retention and access policy; already downloaded copies are outside service revocation.

cases.job: Keep reviewed evidence stable across reruns
procedure: Use a controlled model endpoint A that returns the positive relation and retain the complete bundle.
Repeat with endpoint B returning no assertions, holding source, target and model name constant.
Remove only the fixture response cache, then rerun with a zero-call budget.
expected: The first reviewed bundle remains retrievable with its original bytes.
Different contents or assessment context are distinguishable by immutable evidence identity.
Budget refusal is explicit and does not destroy a prior complete artefact.

cases.job: Answer a multi-hop question and abstain when evidence is absent
procedure: Ask which checklist Alpha's maintainer uses for release review.
Ask for Alpha's annual maintenance cost, which is absent from the corpus.
Inspect every asserted relationship and supporting source.
expected: Checklist Epsilon is supported by both supplied relationships.
The cost answer states that evidence is absent, without inventing a number or citation.

cases.job: Complete a useful correction and reconstruct the result
procedure: A participant finds the outdated requirement, proposes a correction and has a second participant review it.
Apply, restart and retrieve the corrected answer.
Export the corpus and decision evidence, then reconstruct them in an isolated environment using the declared export/import procedure.
Repeat comparable tasks with the manual Git/document-search baseline, counterbalancing order.
expected: The corrected answer and precise reviewed change remain connected after restart and reconstruction.
Record all author, reviewer and operator effort, including failed attempts and setup.
Missing reconstruction support is declared unsupported; no portability claim follows from export alone.
